data: Great game, even better with mods
While it's not perfect, it still has a good story, very fun mechanics, and a lot of replay value
Despite that, really fun game, good story, would recommend
All in all, this game is awesome and well worth the money
I highly recommend XCOM 2 it's fun, engaging, and challenging
the game becomes unplayable and you just wasted your money
the chance mechanics are just not for me
Uninstalled again and unfortunately can't get a refund for this shit

Animations are choppy, characters are bland and all look the same, story feels generic and boring
The game balance is completely broken
it crashes (permentently) through steam on multiple occasions
I've had the game freeze/crash on me 3 times in the first 9 hours
this game is an absolute mess with many antipatterns and half-baked gimmicks that make gameplay frustrating:
The arbitrary time limits contribute absolutely nothing to the story or gameplay
Controls dont work and everything falls off the screen at your monitors resolution
I don't know if it's because I downloaded all of the DLC instead of starting with the base game,
Items are expensive to craft, especially if you're saving supplies to hire new guys
Also "integrated DLC" doesn't mean "enable all", it means "skip story missions and just give me the content with no context"
the modders have made this game 9
Do yourself a favor and download mods for better cover and prevent AI cheating before getting too frustrated

It's a decent game, but the real fun (in my opinion) is in the modding. So many silly or cool combinations and alterations to be made, and Long War of the Chosen is... an experience. At the very least, worth getting on sale. Note that it is somewhat prone to crashes, and look up some guides before modding, if modding is something you're new to. I'm new to it, and it went rather easily despite a couple of really simple mistakes that could have been avoided.
If you liked the first game, you will by chance like this too. New game elements blend with the old making a super fun, rich gaming experience. Also a lot of rage, sadness and dispair like all x com.

game is trash. you take your time planning every move just to get shot though when you try to move.the enemy on overwatch 75% of the time and they miss about 25% of the time only,building cars tanks dont mean nothing, you gone catch them alien bullets no matter what. another thing your team is basically running around blindfolded, they miss he broad side of a barn at point blank consistently tho.I mean if you dont know what rage quit is buy this game.

This game is extremely challenging. I still can't play at the higher difficulties. Some will be put off by the level of concentration it demands, but i think it will mostly go appreciated. I certainly do, and I hope you will as well. That being said, the game isn't perfect. There are times you may find the game to be more stupid than challenging, by either the way the enemy behaves or by how a mission works, in which case you will find yourself using exploits to complete certain tasks (like tiresomely sending your units around a section of a map to avoid a group of enemies for a stealth/rescue mission). These drawbacks are noteworthy and unfortunate, but I would still say the game is overall still worth playing. I would just advise players (especially new ones) not to feel bad for playing at lower difficulties. You may have to before you understand the game enough to play at the higher difficulties. Thanks, and good luck, Commanders.

This is likely one of the greatest tactical games of all time. That said, 2K can't keep their launchers working to save their lives. They have been in the habit of breaking the damn thing on a weekly, sometimes daily basis, so while I would love to recommend this based on how awesome the game it, I'm afraid I must warn people away from it. 2K needs to get their poop in a group and quit breaking the products we paid for.
Great and challenging single-player game. Very good replayability with the Steam Workshop, Multiplayer is terrible/dead but possible co-op mods coming in the future.

Many friends are having to futz with whatever this heaping trash pile of a launcher is that has no reason to stay open in the background of my game. People also suspect said launcher is collecting user data which is already shady af.
I love the game to death. I do not have love for decisions made by suits who know nothing about the clientele and people who mod their games. If they were smart, they wouldn't have replaced a working part with one cheaper and shadier than the licensed businessman who knew what he doing in the first place. Now we got Jose Guarrez 2K launcher perma running in the background doing God knows what and has already busted half of the mods trying to load on most other people's rigs and looking through things he shouldn't.
You don't replace a working part with one that is less qualified and capable for cheaper. That's shady, it's cheap, and it's going to cost you money in all runs of the game. Trusted customers trust was sold off for some cheap 2 bit change that was unnecessary and likely will not buy your product in the future.
Get your shi t together.

I wish there was something in between yes and no, because it's very reluctantly that I recommend the game.

Overall and compared to the average game, it's a great game, no doubt.
Compared to the greatest game, like for me Darkest Dungeon, or to some lesser extent Slay the Spire, it's definitely not there. It got huge qualities, but overall, and similar to xcom 1, the opacity of the rules, the fact that you basically either have to reload like crazy or are required to look for info on the web or youtube even when playing lower difficulties (just completed it in Veteran) makes it more frustrating than enjoyable.
On a side note, also expected a deeper and more sophisticated story than xcom 1. Instead, the beginning especially with the tutorial is great, but mid game and late game is very boring and lacks surprises.

So I would say overall, if you got lots of time to spare and love the genre of this kind of game, sure, jump on it especially if the game is cheap.

But otherwise, it might bring you more frustration than enjoyment overall.

The game starts with the aliens in control of the world's governments, in a brutally repressive regime that pretends to be helpful and benevolent. As X-COM you work from the shadows and you have to organize and lead the resistance. It's a nice twist on the classic X-COM formula. And It's a good mood for 2020.

I found this game much more difficult than its direct predecessor. In particular, if I messed up and got my squad wiped in a mission, I never really recovered. The loss of resources and experienced soldiers was too great, while the aliens still kept getting more powerful, so I lost more men in future missions too and it just became a death spiral. Since I'm too proud to play on easy, I only started doing well on my 7th campaign.

One of the best and most addicting tactical strategy games out there. Not too complicated or overtly difficult can be enjoyed by both newbies and veterans of the genre alike. This is their peak, the next game in the series "XCOM Chimera Squad" is garbage.

Great strategic gameplay. Scratches a certain itch that you can't find anywhere else. Bigger and more sprawling than the first, but a bit less focused. Still, an amazing game. Strongly recommend.

Countless hour playing it heavily modded.
So satisfying to build my dream squad and make up head-canon stories for my squad.

Cons:
took 300 hours of my life.

Ever since the new 2k launcher I have been entirely unable to enjoy this game. Initially, just being unable to use the mods I enjoyed was tolerable but now I can't even launch the game as the 2k launcher crashes instantly whenever I try to start it. Fuck 2k. The launcher was fine when WOTC came out, give it back.

Very fun and dynamic game that includes building a homebase, establishing a global resistance, strategic battles, and more. Heck of a lot of fun when I want something mindless to jump into and then usually immediately after a battle I have to be pause or come back to see the story unfold in a very fluid and organic way!

A truly great tactics game completely undermined by a few bad game mechanics and a truly awful RNG system. The players decisions, good or bad, are so disconnected from the outcome of a mission that victory feels hollow and defeat feels undeserved. The RNG mechanic plays the primary role in deciding how your game will go and if you can accept that then you will probably really enjoy XCOM 2. But if like me you prefer that the games difficulty stems from other sources instead of primarily RNG then you will be disappointed.

One of the best round based games I played. I was a huge fan of the old JA and JA2 games but since then I never found any round based games that were able to enjoy me. This one is different and has some ridiculously hard difficult options, which is great.

I love this game. Now, I am not happy about some features from the original game from CAPCOM. Reducing the amount to six player max in a squad, the characters with psychic powers must be a rookie and not able to give those characters different positions, for example, a sniper, and not being able to sell weapons from the aliens' battles.
The base game is really really good! The WoTC DLC makes it even better!! The mod scene puts this game in S-tier!!!
Xcom has always been a favorite! Personalizing your squad adds a special connection for you to your units. Enjoy!!

Love the game and keep coming back when I can't find another one that quite scratches the same itch. People complain about the rng but the game gives you all the information you need to succeed and it is very satisfying mastering the game to the point where even bad luck cannot stop you.

The best turn based tactical comabat game i have played still in 2026. The 1st one is great as well, play it. Play this. This genre needs more Ace products like this... not the shells we have been getting. Nothing beats setting up an ambush in this game.
Amazing strategy game, great mechanics, good visuals. Plenty of replayablity. Probably a bit dated by now but still remains fun to play.

XCOM on steroids.
If you liked XCOM:EU, then you simply have to play this. They have improved practically everything about the original.

Pros:
- Looks better
- Plays faster
- It's more challenging then before
- Better customization
- New enemy types
- Steam workshop

Cons:
- Early game may be too challenging for some (Events occur too quickly)
- Grenades too strong (Grenadiers are OP)
- Boring selection of weapons, 1 type for every tier for each class... (3 tiers total)
- On rails, there is no real choice what to do next
- In missions: Free alien activation when you expose them (makes you save scum, or move very slowly)

8/10, would kill aliens again.

The game is one of the greatest tactical turn-based games ever made. Nearly perfect (even with the hilarious animations when you "miss" at 94% accuracy). Patience, smart planning, and understanding line-of-site and how enemies react is almost always rewarded (90% of the time, heh).

The new 2K launcher, however, can go jump in a wood chipper.
Long story short, a Fun Turn-Based Tactical Game. The vanilla one is already fun, but with many awesome contents from the modding community, this one is one of the best strategy game ever.

Expansion war of the chosen is worse expasion, too expensive, mod Long War brings much more fun and much smarter than kill alien like predator. Unfortunately the zombies are give absurd lag and the fog worsened even more.
A advice look for who produced the long war and engage to make a better expansion.

If you like turn based combat, this game is incredible, and one of the best ever made. I don't really understand the negative review due to it being "too hard". I don't find it too difficult at all, and I'm a perfectionist. I saw people complain about a mission taking 2 hours, and not being able to beat it without losing a soldier, but you are supposed to lose soldiers. Losing and replacing soldiers is part of the game. You can even visit the bar, where you guys drink to the fallen soldiers. I try not to lose any guys if possible, but sometimes you just need to accept losing a guy here and there. I also like how long it takes to do each battle. Who wants to just easily run through short battles? I usually find turn based combat too easy, but this on regular difficulty is just easy enough. If it's tough and turn based games aren't your strong suit. just play on easy mode. I'm sad I didn't pick a harder difficulty. Games like this should be a challenge.

561 hours played so far and I just started a new campaign last week in a game that is 9 years old!
What else can i say about this masterpiece of a game!?
It is a game that with all the amazing mods that are around can be played for 10 more years from now on.
YOU make your own story in this game. Each new campaign is different each time you play, and as i said with the mods around, you basically play multiple games at once using only the core engine of Xcom 2.

A must play in life. Period.

XCOM 2 is a fantastic turn-based strategy game that builds upon everything great from the first installment. The graphical design is stunning, the controls feel smooth, and the atmosphere keeps you on edge throughout the campaign.

The variety of missions and new soldier classes add depth and replayability. The game truly captures the feeling of leading a desperate resistance against an overwhelming alien force.

However, the camera can be frustrating at times. But despite that, XCOM 2 remains one of the best strategy games ever made.

Rating: 5/5
its good. but for the most part youre better off skipping the main game and play the better version of war of the chosen. I did the main game then WotC and can confirm it feels alot better.

Even as a long-time XCom player, I was not as immediately engrossed in this as I was Enemy Within. It's very good and I recommend it fully but if you love the original you should be prepared for this to feel different.

Helluva game! Brings same great fundamentals of XCOM EU and spices things up. WOTC added nice elements to swarm you with like EW did in earlier game. Shen's mech from DLC also a nice addition as well as the bads from Alien Hunters DLC which offers great armor as rewards to boot.

Graphics are good, bad guys are diverse, though some return from original. Also having significant weapon mods is a plus for this game.

I basically stopped all my other gaming to focus on this one for a week and it was super fun start to end. If you like tactical gameplay, simply get this!

Overall: 10/10
Awesome game, I have put in many hours, and still very much enjoy it after years of play. I do wish XCOM 3 would come out already.

Highly Recommended! 

its a fantastic turn-based strategy game that puts you in command of a ragtag resistance fighting for humanity's freedom. It's challenging, rewarding, and oh-so-satisfying when your squad pulls off an impossible victory.
Best game of the genre. I have been trying to find an equal ever since but to no avail. If you like tactical rpg, this is your game, you won't have any regrets.

XCOM2 is what XCOM should have been from the start. No more aliens appearing out of nowhere with no warning, and you have a few more options on how to approach situations even from the start of the campaign. There is even more room for maneuver. Unfortunately, like all Firaxis titles, it is full of gamey mechanics, for example: you have to do research so you can remove weapon mods without destroying them. It is very cool that the weapons have mods and everything, but anything that could be turned into a game mechanic, to make the game look more complex, got turned into a mechanic. In addition, it’s a bit silly that not all soldiers have handguns.

XCOM2 the campaign is funneled through the story so it may appear that you don’t have as much agency as you expected. Don’t worry though, the game is full with options and there is plenty to do. The main DLC adds even more and overall the game feels complete and satisfying.

Like all XCOM titles, the game is at its best when played in Ironman mode (no “scum saving”). But there are so many game mechanics and things that you could greatly benefit from knowing in advance, not to mention the occasion bug, that pure Ironman might be very time consuming. So maybe a solution to this might be a self-imposed Ironman where you can only load saved games when you encounter new game mechanics.

I have no idea who greenlit this on the 2k side but they should be fired. Forcing users to use a worse launcher when the previous one worked fine is unacceptable.

I liked XCOM:Enemy Unknown. I have tried XCOM2 twice now: first time over a year ago and after installing 30 mods to remove all the frustrating animations and and "out of control" stuff, I just could not take how imblanced and frustrating this game feels.

Now I tried again and gave it another 7 hours. But I can't stand it. Half the game is loading screens and animations, 25% is fun. Rest is the imblanced difficulty messing you over again and again.

I'm just getting frustrated. It feels like a second job.
Great game but insanely frustrating VAT system. You need true patience which I don't have so that's it for me lol

Game didn't age well in regards to comparison to say Phoenix Point, but is still better balanced than Phoenix Point that has literal game breaking bugs at its final boss fight, and also horrible balance for players of varying experience and focus level.

Phoenix Point can be saved by mods but must be installed by 3rd party, where as Xcom has Steam Workshop so that's a plus.

That being said Xcom requires 2K launcher be open, has some weird antivirus reactions and also seems to have some game freezes (maybe I need a verification or reinstall)

The graphics are good, if a little over the top with animations etc, but it's a decent story and world setting. Honestly I wish I could take the best aspects from Xcom 2 and Phoenix Point and make a better game over-all.

Legacy Hub stuff doesn't seem to work though

Also could load the other challenges.

If you can get this game working without crashes etc, then I'd say its an okay game.
This game is super fun and super challenging, definitely worth the money. 10/10, would buy again.

I really wanted to love this game. I had heard of Xcom in the past: but never played till this games predecessor(one of the best games I have ever played and hands down better than this game). It was actually going to be the first game I ever did a "let's play" for. That came to a really quick end when I was smashed in the face with horrible loads, graphics issues, bugs on top of bugs, ect... It was so bad that I couldn't bring myself to upload the footage. Before anyone asks I was running a GTX 960 and an FX-6300 processor(well above the max requirements for the game). Here we are over a year later and nothing has changed. Save your time and money by skipping this one.

2k added a new launcher... to a game that already had a working one... that in no way was needed... cool great awesome it broke things for others but not me although it may have broke things for me as i am not seeing some mods from steam in the list which didn't even add to much :T thanks a lot for continuing the trend of ruining perfectly fine games.

A wonderful original game is taken to another level by war of the chosen, well worth replaying.

Amazing game overall. Fantastic representation of the turn based strategy genre and I highly recommend a purchase. I played on xbox one long before I purchased it on steam so in truth I have over about 150 hours played. The only complaint with this newest addition to the franchise is the introduction of dark events. It is hard to keep them under control on the higher difficulties and you sort of have to pick and choose how to slow them down since it is virtually impossible to prevent them. This, however, is easily fixed with the Long War 2 mod available on the workshop and this mod alone has caused me to put in another 6 hours in the first day and a half of owning the game. There are plenty of other mods available that overhaul soldier appearances and even a Warhammer 40k overhaul mod if that's your mojo. Overall it is a great game worth catching on sale for sure. I wouldn't recommend paying the full price unless you're desperate since the game goes on sale once every couple months.

Great game, first play was amazing, started another one right after and its been nothing but game breaking crashes if its modded,,, same with if its not modded, otherwise worth it if this issue doesn't happen with you

XCOM2 is not flawless. It has bugs, including very unfortunate ones (isn't it fun to find out that your beloved colonel Ranger, who has recently become Death, the Destroyer of Mobs, and was knocked unconscious, can't be picked up and will have to go MIA?). It has way too much unskippable animation—even in the faster mode you'll still see "cinematic" overwatch triggers, and managing the base can get a bit tedious due to, once again, animations. Sometimes you can fight the cursor for a minute while trying to make your Ranger attack the enemy from the right side.

But these are all extremely minor gripes, of course. The core gamplay of XCOM has long become legendary, and it's as slick and fun as ever, with clear distinctive visuals, great level design, and the ever-beloved option to design your whole extended family into not-quite-space marines and watch them die excruciating deaths due to missing three 90%-chance shots in a row.

The price tag is intimidating, but if turn-based tactical games appeal to you in the slightest, you definitely should buy this.

Then again, you most likely already have.
